newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate plunges on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate plunges on firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down a sharp 210 basis points at 21.40 percent on Wednesday in response to a stabler peso and on lower liquidity pressures, dealers said.

Wednesday saw the cutoff date for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank. Dealers said most banks had squared positions and thus speculation on demand for liquidity eased.
"The market was stable... Today was the cutoff date, another accountancy period starts tomorrow and that eases speculative pressure," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 1.2 centavos stronger at 7.9640/7.9660 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 3.780 billion pesos from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales, and six repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended down 225 basis points at 21.90 percent.
Liquidity of 3.437 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
